characterList.description: A tall, thin man with short gray hair and a receding hairline. He is wearing a blue shirt, a dark suit jacket, and dark pants.
characterList.name: Johan Rockstrom

content_metadata.description: A video presentation by Johan Rockstrom discussing a new perspective on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), utilizing a "wedding cake" model to highlight their interconnectedness.

qAndA.answer: He compares the 17 SDG icons arranged in a grid to a "Swedish smörgåsbord" implying that people might pick and choose their favorites rather than addressing them as interconnected goals.
qAndA.question: What visual metaphor does Johan use to illustrate the potential pitfall of approaching the SDGs in a fragmented way?
What is the name given to the new integrated framework for understanding the SDGs presented by Johan?

qAndA.answer: Those related to the environment: Goal 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), Goal 13 (Climate Action), Goal 14 (Life Below Water), and Goal 15 (Life on Land).
qAndA.question: Which SDGs are considered non-negotiable in the "wedding cake" framework?

qAndA.answer: It injects humor and self-awareness, acknowledging the temptation to address the SDGs selectively instead of holistically.
qAndA.question: How does Johan's comparison of the SDGs to a "Swedish smörgåsbord" contribute to the presentation?

qAndA.answer: The biosphere, represented by goals 6, 13, 14, and 15.
qAndA.question: According to the video, what is the base of the "wedding cake" model?

narrativeProgression.description: Johan emphasizes the scientific imperative for planetary stewardship.
The SDGs are introduced as a roadmap for achieving this stewardship, highlighting their unprecedented scope and ambition.
Johan presents a new framework for understanding the interconnected nature of the SDGs, emphasizing the non-negotiable environmental goals as the foundation.

text_to_speech: The science now supports that we do have to become planetary stewards. I'm so glad that that has been a core of the thematic discussion here. Planetary stewardship is clearly about recognizing the sustainable development goals. We've never had, can you imagine, we've never had a roadmap for the first time with aspirational socioeconomic goals based on equity, based on universality for all co-citizens in the world within planetary boundaries, and that is quite extraordinary. The Millennium Development Goals were about poverty and were not about sustainability and did not put pressure on us who live way, way beyond our means of exploiting unsustainably planet Earth, but we as scientists have recognized that there's a risk with this chart. It looks like a Swedish smorgasbord to be honest. (laughing) You can kinda cherry pick your favorites and then go off and deliver on it. So we have translated this to a new integrated framework, which we call the Wedding Cake, which is stating very clearly that there are some nonnegotiable sustainable development goals. Goal six on water, goal 13 on climate, goal 14 on oceans, goal 15 on biodiversity, and that these are the safe operating space within which we can have a just, equitable, social inclusive development attaining the social aspirational goals, the economy, and those goals being means of achievement, and that governance is the way to get our partnerships together.

youtube_description:
A pathway for planetary stewardship. Watch the full talk: https://ehf.nz/johan18b

Johan Rockström is the founding director of the Stockholm Resilience Centre (http://www.stockholmresilience.org) and incoming director of Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (https://www.pik-potsdam.de/). 

Filmed at New Frontiers (https://www.newfrontiers.nz) in New Zealand, hosted by the Edmund Hillary Fellowship (https://www.ehf.org).
